gallery.title: File:Broadway in Westchester around 1900.jpg
gallery.description: Depicts Curley's Monumental Granite and Marble Works, a major stone-working establishment on Broadway in North Tarrytown (now Sleepy Hollow) that made tombstones for the nearby Sleepy Hollow Cemetery. It was located in the northernmost section of Broadway (Albany Post Road) in North Tarrytown, near the cemetery (this photograph was taken at the turn of the 20th century, before the road was improved with macadam surfacing). As of 2026, the building still existed, repurposed as an auto body shop.
